Name: Musée du Louvre #1
Description: World's largest art museum holding Mona Lisa, Venus de Milo, and centuries of royal history.
Why Go: Unrivaled destination for world art, classical sculpture, and iconic architectural glass pyramid.

Name: Musée d'Orsay #2
Description: Stunning Beaux-Arts train station filled with Impressionist and Post-Impressionist masterpieces.
Why Go: Essential gallery featuring Monet, Van Gogh, Degas, and Renoir along the Seine.
Address: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, 75007 Paris

Name: Centre Pompidou #3
Description: High-tech architectural marvel showcasing premier modern and contemporary art collections.
Why Go: Iconic inside-out building offering high-caliber modern art and panoramic rooftop vistas.

Name: Sainte-Chapelle #4
Description: Gothic royal chapel famed for breathtaking 13th-century stained-glass windows depicting biblical stories.
Why Go: A soaring sanctuary bathed in kaleidoscopic light and jewel-toned Gothic architecture.
Neighborhood: Île de la Cité & Île Saint-Louis

Name: Musée de l'Orangerie #5
Description: Intimate gallery in Tuileries Garden built specifically to house Monet's immense Water Lilies murals.
Why Go: Serene oval rooms bathed in natural light showcasing Monet's immersive masterworks.

Name: Musée Rodin #6
Description: Elegant 18th-century mansion and sculpture garden housing Auguste Rodin's masterpiece 'The Thinker'.
Why Go: Tranquil roses and bronze sculptures scattered across lush historic grounds.

Name: Palais Garnier - Opéra National de Paris #7
Description: Opulent 19th-century opera house with gilded foyers, Chagall ceiling painting, and velvet auditorium.
Why Go: Architectural masterpiece of French Neo-Baroque drama and world-class opera performances.
Specific Website URL: Palais Garnier - Opéra National de Paris Website

Name: Musée Carnavalet #8
Description: Dedicated museum of Parisian history located in two adjacent aristocratic mansions in Le Marais.
Why Go: Fascinating journey through Paris history from prehistoric times to Marcel Proust's bedroom.

Name: Panthéon #9
Description: Neoclassical mausoleum holding tombs of France's legendary figures including Voltaire, Hugo, and Curie.
Why Go: Majestic dome overlooking Latin Quarter featuring Foucault's pendulum and sweeping city views.

Name: Fondation Louis Vuitton #10
Description: Frank Gehry-designed glass building shaped like sailing ship, housing cutting-edge contemporary art.
